title: Pullback of coherent formal modules
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of Noetherian schemes, $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal O_Y$ a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals and $\mathcal I=f^{-1}\mathcal J\cdot\mathcal O_X$. (1) For an object $(\mathcal G_n)$ of $\mathit{Coh}(Y,\mathcal J)$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] the system $(f^*\mathcal G_n)$ [def-pc-module-pullback], with the pulled back transition maps, is an object of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$; this defines a functor $f^*:\mathit{Coh}(Y,\mathcal J)\to\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$. (2) For a coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module $\mathcal G$ [pqf-def-coherent] there is a natural isomorphism $f^*(\mathcal G^\wedge)\cong(f^*\mathcal G)^\wedge$; when $f$ is the inclusion of an open subscheme $U\subseteq Y$, $f^*$ is restriction to $U$, so $(\mathcal G^\wedge)|_U=(\mathcal G|_U)^\wedge$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0887 (lemma-inverse-systems-pullback), first assertion and the computation in its proof; for (2) the identity f^*(G^) = (f^*G)^ used in the proof of Lemma 088B (lemma-inverse-systems-push-pull)

proof.text: (The ideal $\mathcal I$.) By [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-ideal-quotient] (1), $\mathcal I=f^{-1}\mathcal J\cdot\mathcal O_X$ (the image of $f^*\mathcal J\to f^*\mathcal O_Y\to\mathcal O_X$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal]) is a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals of $\mathcal O_X$, so, $X$ being Noetherian, the category $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ of [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] is defined; and by part (2) of the same node $\mathcal J^n\mathcal O_X=\mathcal I^n$ for every $n\ge1$. Each $\mathcal J^n$ is a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals of $\mathcal O_Y$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module, step 1], so the node applies to $\mathcal J^n$ in place of $\mathcal J$: for every quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module $\mathcal G$ and $n\ge1$, with $q^n_{\mathcal G}:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G/\mathcal J^n\mathcal G$ and $p^n_{\mathcal G}:f^*\mathcal G\to f^*\mathcal G/\mathcal I^nf^*\mathcal G$ the quotient maps, $f^*q^n_{\mathcal G}$ is an epimorphism with kernel $\mathcal I^nf^*\mathcal G$ and there is a unique isomorphism $\sigma^n_{\mathcal G}:f^*\mathcal G/\mathcal I^nf^*\mathcal G\to f^*(\mathcal G/\mathcal J^n\mathcal G)$ with $\sigma^n_{\mathcal G}\circ p^n_{\mathcal G}=f^*q^n_{\mathcal G}$, natural in $\mathcal G$. (This is the computation $f^*(\mathcal G/\mathcal J^n\mathcal G)=f^*\mathcal G/f^{-1}\mathcal J^nf^*\mathcal G$ of the Stacks proof, where the ideals $\mathcal I$ and $\mathcal J$ are interchanged by a misprint.)

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 0887 (lemma-inverse-systems-pullback), the displayed computation

proof.text: (The terms are coherent.) Let $(\mathcal G_n)$ be an object of $\mathit{Coh}(Y,\mathcal J)$. Each $\mathcal G_n$ is coherent on the locally Noetherian $Y$, hence quasi-coherent of finite type [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth] (Stacks 01XZ). Then $f^*\mathcal G_n$ is quasi-coherent [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent] (Modules, Lemma 01BG) and of finite type [lem-weil-pbc-support-pullback-finite-type] (3) (Modules, Lemma 01B6), so it is coherent since $X$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]. The pulled-back transition maps $f^*t_n:f^*\mathcal G_{n+1}\to f^*\mathcal G_n$ are $\mathcal O_X$-linear, so $(f^*\mathcal G_n,f^*t_n)$ is an inverse system of coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-pc-module-pullback].

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 0887 ('f^*: Coh(O_Y) -> Coh(O_X)'); Lemma 01XZ (lemma-coherent-Noetherian)

proof.text: ($\mathcal I^nf^*\mathcal G_n=0$.) Since $\mathcal J^n\mathcal G_n=0$, the quotient map $q^n_{\mathcal G_n}:\mathcal G_n\to\mathcal G_n/\mathcal J^n\mathcal G_n$ is the cokernel of the zero map, an isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module, step 3]; so $f^*q^n_{\mathcal G_n}$ is an isomorphism (a functor preserves isomorphisms). By step 1 its kernel is $\mathcal I^nf^*\mathcal G_n$, which is therefore $0$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 0887; the conditions defining Coh(X, I) in Section 0EHN (section-coherent-formal)

proof.text: (The transition maps induce isomorphisms.) By the definition of $\mathit{Coh}(Y,\mathcal J)$ the transition map factors as $t_n=\bar t_n\circ q^n_{\mathcal G_{n+1}}$ with $\bar t_n:\mathcal G_{n+1}/\mathcal J^n\mathcal G_{n+1}\to\mathcal G_n$ an isomorphism. Hence $f^*t_n=f^*(\bar t_n)\circ f^*q^n_{\mathcal G_{n+1}}=f^*(\bar t_n)\circ\sigma^n_{\mathcal G_{n+1}}\circ p^n_{\mathcal G_{n+1}}$ (step 1). The map $\overline{f^*t_n}:f^*\mathcal G_{n+1}/\mathcal I^nf^*\mathcal G_{n+1}\to f^*\mathcal G_n$ induced by $f^*t_n$ (it exists and is unique by [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module, step 4], using step 3 here) is characterized by $\overline{f^*t_n}\circ p^n_{\mathcal G_{n+1}}=f^*t_n$; so $\overline{f^*t_n}=f^*(\bar t_n)\circ\sigma^n_{\mathcal G_{n+1}}$, a composite of two isomorphisms. With steps 2 and 3, $(f^*\mathcal G_n)$ satisfies condition (1) of [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]: it is an object of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 0887: 'f^*G_n = f^*(G_{n+1}/J^nG_{n+1}) = f^*G_{n+1}/I^n f^*G_{n+1}, hence the pullback of a system is a system'

proof.text: (The functor.) For a morphism $(\alpha_n):(\mathcal G_n)\to(\mathcal G'_n)$ of $\mathit{Coh}(Y,\mathcal J)$, $t'_n\alpha_{n+1}=\alpha_nt_n$ gives $f^*t'_n\circ f^*\alpha_{n+1}=f^*\alpha_n\circ f^*t_n$ since $f^*$ is a functor [def-pc-module-pullback]; so $(f^*\alpha_n)$ is a morphism of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$, and $f^*(\mathrm{id})=\mathrm{id}$, $f^*(\beta\alpha)=f^*\beta\circ f^*\alpha$ componentwise. Hence $(\mathcal G_n)\mapsto(f^*\mathcal G_n)$, $(\alpha_n)\mapsto(f^*\alpha_n)$ is a functor $f^*:\mathit{Coh}(Y,\mathcal J)\to\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module, step 4]. This proves (1).

(Part (2): $f^*(\mathcal G^\wedge)\cong(f^*\mathcal G)^\wedge$.) Let $\mathcal G$ be coherent; $\mathcal G^\wedge=(\mathcal G/\mathcal J^n\mathcal G,r_n)$ is an object of $\mathit{Coh}(Y,\mathcal J)$ with $r_n\circ q^{n+1}_{\mathcal G}=q^n_{\mathcal G}$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module, step 5], so $f^*(\mathcal G^\wedge)=(f^*(\mathcal G/\mathcal J^n\mathcal G),f^*r_n)$ is an object of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ by (1); and $f^*\mathcal G$ is coherent (step 2), so $(f^*\mathcal G)^\wedge=(f^*\mathcal G/\mathcal I^nf^*\mathcal G,\pi_n)$ with $\pi_n\circ p^{n+1}=p^n$. The isomorphisms $\sigma^n=\sigma^n_{\mathcal G}$ of step 1 commute with the transition maps: $f^*r_n\circ\sigma^{n+1}\circ p^{n+1}=f^*r_n\circ f^*q^{n+1}=f^*q^n=\sigma^n\circ p^n=\sigma^n\circ\pi_n\circ p^{n+1}$, and $p^{n+1}$ is an epimorphism, so $f^*r_n\circ\sigma^{n+1}=\sigma^n\circ\pi_n$. Hence $(\sigma^n)_n:(f^*\mathcal G)^\wedge\to f^*(\mathcal G^\wedge)$ is a morphism of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ whose components are isomorphisms; the componentwise inverses also commute with the transition maps, so it is an isomorphism. For $\mathcal O_Y$-linear $u:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G'$ between coherent modules, the naturality of $\sigma^n$ in [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-ideal-quotient] (3) says $\sigma^n_{\mathcal G'}\circ\overline{f^*u}=f^*(u_n)\circ\sigma^n_{\mathcal G}$, i.e. $(\sigma^n)$ is natural: $f^*(u^\wedge)\circ(\sigma^n_{\mathcal G})=(\sigma^n_{\mathcal G'})\circ(f^*u)^\wedge$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 088B (lemma-inverse-systems-push-pull), the identification f^*(G^) = (f^*G)^; computation of the proof of Lemma 0887

proof.text: (Open subschemes.) Let $f:U\to Y$ be the inclusion of an open subscheme. Then $f^*\cong(-)|_U$ naturally [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-module-pullback-restriction], and $\epsilon_f:f^*\mathcal O_Y\to\mathcal O_U$ is an isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-structure-sheaf]; both $\epsilon_f\circ\kappa_{\mathcal O_Y}$ and the identity of $\mathcal O_Y|_U=\mathcal O_U$ correspond to $f^\sharp$ under the adjunction, so they agree. By naturality of $\kappa$, the composite $f^*\mathcal J\to f^*\mathcal O_Y\to\mathcal O_U$ is identified with the inclusion $\mathcal J|_U\to\mathcal O_U$, so $\mathcal I=f^{-1}\mathcal J\cdot\mathcal O_U=\mathcal J|_U$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal]. Thus (2) reads $(\mathcal G^\wedge)|_U\cong(\mathcal G|_U)^\wedge$, the completion on $U$ taken with respect to $\mathcal J|_U$; concretely $(\mathcal J^n\mathcal G)|_U=(\mathcal J|_U)^n(\mathcal G|_U)$ [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections] (3), applied inductively to $\mathcal J^n=\mathcal J\cdot\mathcal J^{n-1}$ and to $\mathcal J^n\mathcal G$, and restriction to $U$ preserves cokernels.

split_report.summary: Statement kept (it is the first assertion of Stacks 0887 without right exactness and the flat case, which no user cites, plus the identity f^*(G^) = (f^*G)^ of the proof of 088B). Proof in seven steps following the computation of the 0887 proof: the extended ideal and its powers, the quotient computation f^*(G/J^nG) = f^*G/I^n f^*G (new node lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-ideal-quotient, the right-exactness argument of the Stacks proof, unsplit), coherence of f^*G_n (01XZ, 01BG via the closed node, 01B6 via lem-weil-pbc-support-pullback-finite-type), I^n f^*G_n = 0, the transition isomorphisms, functoriality, part (2) with compatibility with transition maps and naturality, and the open-immersion case (I = J|_U). The Stacks display has I and J interchanged (misprint). The brief's guess 01BG is the quasi-coherent pullback lemma, not a coherent one; Stacks has no separate lemma 'pullback of coherent is coherent' for Noetherian schemes, it is 01BG + 01B6 + 01XZ.
